<script>

// "Save figure" links (see plot_figure_as_html in the library): the figure is the element just before the clicked link
function saveSvgFigure(clickedEl, downloadName) {

	var svgEl = clickedEl.previousElementSibling;
  svgEl.setAttribute("xmlns", "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg");
  var svgData = svgEl.outerHTML;
  var preface = '<?xml version="1.0" standalone="no"?>\r\n';
  var svgBlob = new Blob([preface, svgData], {type:"image/svg+xml;charset=utf-8"});
  var svgUrl = URL.createObjectURL(svgBlob);
  
  _createThenClickImageLink(svgUrl, downloadName);
}

function savePngFigure(clickedEl, downloadName) {
	var imgEl = clickedEl.previousElementSibling;
	
	_createThenClickImageLink(imgEl.src, downloadName);
}

function _createThenClickImageLink(imageUrl, downloadName) {
  var downloadLink = document.createElement("a");
  downloadLink.href = imageUrl;
  downloadLink.download = downloadName;
  
  document.body.appendChild(downloadLink);
  downloadLink.click(); // triggers image download
  document.body.removeChild(downloadLink);
}
</script>

```{r file_import, include=FALSE}
##Importing raw data file given as a parameter and parses the names of the samples included##

data <- read.csv(params$quantif_file, check.names = F, sep="\t")

# Condition and replicate of each sample (in the order of the sample columns), when an experimental design is given
sample_conditions <- NULL
sample_replicates <- NULL

if(file.exists(params$design_exp)){
  expDesign <- read.csv(params$design_exp, header = T, sep="\t")

  # Checking that the experimental design and the quantification table are consistent
  validate_inputs(data, expDesign, derived_suffixes = character(0))

  group_ids <- unique(expDesign$Condition)
  
  abundance_repbio = data.frame(data$Id)
  colnames(abundance_repbio) = "Id"
  
  identification_type_repbio = data.frame(data$Id)
  colnames(identification_type_repbio) = "Id"
  
  for(group in group_ids){
    
    sub = subset(expDesign,expDesign$Condition==group)
    
    for (rBio in unique(sub$repBio)){
      
      samples_intensities = subset(sub,sub$repBio==rBio)$File
      samples_identification_type = paste0("Identification_type",sub("Intensity","",samples_intensities))
      
      abundance_repbio = cbind(abundance_repbio,data[as.character(samples_intensities)])
      identification_type_repbio = cbind(identification_type_repbio,data[samples_identification_type])
      
      colnames(abundance_repbio)[ncol(abundance_repbio)] = paste0("Intensity_",sub(" ", "", rBio),"_",group)
      colnames(identification_type_repbio)[ncol(identification_type_repbio)] = paste0("Identification_type_",sub(" ", "", rBio),"_",group)
      sample_conditions <- c(sample_conditions, as.character(group))
      sample_replicates <- c(sample_replicates, as.character(rBio))
    }
  }
  
  data = merge.data.frame(data[, 1:3],identification_type_repbio,by="Id")
  data = merge.data.frame(data,abundance_repbio,by="Id")
}
sample_names = colnames(data)[grepl("Intensity",names(data))]
# Sample name without the intensity prefix, as in the identification type columns ("Identification_type_<sample>"):
# ("Intensity_<repBio>_<Condition>" with an experimental design, the input column names otherwise)
sample_names_parsed = sub("^Intensity_", "", sample_names)
parameters <- read.csv(params$parameters, header=T, sep="=")

# write.csv(data, "QC_data.csv", row.names = F)

```


```{r param_parsing}
# ##Parsing parameters##
# as.logical, as.numeric, as.character()
Normalization = as.logical(parameters["Normalization",])
keep_empty_rows = as.logical(parameters["keep_empty_rows",])
format_svg = as.logical(parameters["format_svg",])
coloring_by_group = as.logical(parameters["coloring_by_group",])

# Percentile (in %) of the observed intensities of each sample used as noise level by the imputation (5 if absent)
if ("Imputation.MNAR.percentile" %in% rownames(parameters)) {
  Imputation.MNAR.percentile = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(parameters["Imputation.MNAR.percentile",])))
} else {
  Imputation.MNAR.percentile = 5
  cat("Note: parameter Imputation.MNAR.percentile is absent, 5 is used.\n", file = stderr())
}
if (is.na(Imputation.MNAR.percentile) || Imputation.MNAR.percentile <= 0 || Imputation.MNAR.percentile > 10) {
  stop("Parameter Imputation.MNAR.percentile must be greater than 0 and at most 10 (%).")
}

```

```{r delete_empty_rows}
##If parameter 'Keep empty rows' is false, deletes all empty rows from the data file##

if(keep_empty_rows==FALSE){
  data$na_count = apply(data[grepl("Intensity",names(data))],1,function(x) sum(is.na(x)))
  data = subset(data,data$na_count!=ncol(data[grepl("Intensity",names(data))]))
}

```


```{r find group names}
##Parses sample group names from raw data file##

if(coloring_by_group && file.exists(params$design_exp)){
  
  color_group <- TRUE

  # (the experimental design is shown in the table of the samples, chunk colname_parsing)
  group_names <- unique(expDesign$Condition)

  ######################################################################
  
  # Colours of the conditions, shared with the DA report (condition_colors in the library: Paul Tol "bright" up to 7 conditions)
  group_colors <- condition_colors(length(group_names))
  
  ######################################################################
  
  # Colour of each sample: the colour of its group, in the order of the sample columns
  # (one sample per repBio of each condition, see sample_conditions)
  sample_colors <- group_colors[match(sample_conditions, group_names)]
}else{
  color_group <- FALSE
}

```


```{r colname_parsing, results='asis'}
##Parsing from data file the names of the samples and limits the length of sample names. If sample names > 15 characters, numbers will be used in## 
##the graphic keys##

# Names longer than 15 characters: "<Condition>_<index>" (the samples, one per repBio of each condition, see sample_conditions, numbered
# within their condition in the order of the columns), or S1, S2... without experimental design (display_sample_names, in the library,
# also used by the DA report)
sample_number <- display_sample_names(sample_names_parsed, if (file.exists(params$design_exp)) sample_conditions else NULL)
setnames(data, old=as.character(sample_names),new=sample_number)
sample_names = sample_number
namesDF = data.frame(sample_names_parsed,sample_number)
colnames(namesDF)=c("Sample","Id")

# Table of the samples: name, name in the figures (when shortened), and with an experimental design, the condition, the replicate (repBio)
# and the intensity column(s) of the design (the files of a replicate are combined into one sample)
samples_table <- data.frame(Sample = sample_names_parsed, check.names = FALSE)
if (!identical(sample_number, sample_names_parsed)) samples_table[["Name in the figures"]] <- sample_number
if (length(sample_conditions) == length(sample_names_parsed)) {
  samples_table$Condition <- sample_conditions
  samples_table$Replicate <- sample_replicates
  samples_table[["File(s)"]] <- mapply(function(condition, replicate) {
    paste(sub("^Intensity_", "", expDesign$File[expDesign$Condition == condition & expDesign$repBio == replicate]), collapse = ", ")
  }, sample_conditions, sample_replicates, USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}
samples_kable <- kable(samples_table, format = "html", caption = "Samples", row.names = FALSE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "condensed", full_width = F, position = "left")
# Scroll box when the table is long
cat(if (nrow(samples_table) > 12) scroll_box(samples_kable, height = "300px") else samples_kable)
```

```{r log_transformation}

# Compute log10 values
for (sample in sample_names){
  colname_log = paste0(sample,"_log")
  data[colname_log] <- log10(as.numeric(unlist(data[sample])))
}

# Data parsing to a data frame with a single column containing all the values to plot, and sample in an other column
log_abundance = data[,grepl("_log",names(data))]
colnames(log_abundance) = sample_names
logIntensitiesDF = reshape2::melt(log_abundance)
colnames(logIntensitiesDF) = c("sample","log_intensity")
```

```{r density_plot}
##Creating the data frame for the 'Intensity distribution over all samples' line graph and Intensity distribution in each sample'##

logIntensitiesDF$sample <- factor(logIntensitiesDF$sample, as.character(sample_names))

# Legends of the density plots (before and after normalization), one curve per sample:
# - coloured by condition (color_group: coloring_by_group parameter and an experimental design), the curves have a legend of the
#   conditions (short, whatever the number of samples);
# - otherwise (no design, or coloring_by_group=F), each sample has its own colour: above 12 samples, an inner legend of the samples
#   would take most of the figure, so the density plots have no legend, and a legend panel shared with the box plots is shown under
#   them, with ggplot's default colours (those of the plots)
shared_legend <- !color_group && length(sample_names) > 12
sample_palette <- scales::hue_pal()(length(sample_names))
if (color_group) logIntensitiesDF$condition <- factor(sample_conditions[match(logIntensitiesDF$sample, sample_names)], levels = group_names)

##Framing 'Intensity distribution over all samples' line graph with ggplots##

density <- ggplot() +
  {if (color_group) geom_density(data = logIntensitiesDF, mapping = aes(x=log_intensity,group=sample,color=condition), na.rm = T)
   else geom_density(data = logIntensitiesDF, mapping = aes(x=log_intensity,group=sample,color=sample), na.rm = T)} +
  ggtitle("Intensity distribution over all samples")+
  xlab("log(intensity)")+
  #viridis::scale_color_viridis(alpha=0.6,begin=0.1,end=0.6,discrete = T,breaks=sample_names)+
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=median(na.omit(logIntensitiesDF$log_intensity))), linetype="dashed", size=1)+
  geom_text(mapping=aes(x=median(na.omit(logIntensitiesDF$log_intensity)), y=0, label="median"), size=5, angle=90, vjust=-0.4, hjust=0) +
  {if(color_group) scale_color_manual("Condition", values = setNames(group_colors, group_names))} +
  # Legend of the conditions wrapping on several rows if needed (widths measured, see condition_legend_guide in the library)
  {if (color_group) condition_legend_guide(group_names, 600)} +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size=18),
        axis.title=element_text(size=16),
        axis.text=element_text(size=14),
        legend.text=element_text(size=13),
        legend.title=element_text(size=14)) +
  {if (color_group) theme(legend.position = "bottom")} +
  {if (shared_legend) theme(legend.position = "none")}

##Plotting and printing 'Intensity distribution over all samples' line graph (.svg or .png dependent on set parameters) with download link##

htmltools::HTML(paste0(plot_figure_as_html(density, "Intensity_distribution_over_all_samples", svg = format_svg), "<br>"))

```

```{r boxplots, results='asis'}
# Coloured by condition (color_group), with a legend of the conditions as the density plot; otherwise one colour per sample, no legend.

cat(htmltools::HTML(plot_figure_as_html(violinPlot, "Intensity_distribution_in_each_sample", svg = format_svg)))
figure_note("Distribution of the log10 intensities in each sample, before normalization (violin: density; box: median and quartiles). The medians and the spreads should be similar between samples; differences of the medians are corrected by the normalization.")
```

```{r bar graph, results='asis'}
# Total intensity of each sample: sum of all its observed intensities, before normalization
TotalIntensitiesDF <- data.frame(
  sample = factor(sample_names, levels = sample_names),
  total_intensity = sapply(sample_names, function(s) sum(as.numeric(data[[s]]), na.rm = TRUE)),
  row.names = NULL)

# Bars sorted by total intensity. The colours follow the sample (factor levels in the order of sample_names), not the row order:
# coloured by condition (color_group), with a legend of the conditions as in the identification plot, one colour per sample otherwise
if (color_group) TotalIntensitiesDF$condition <- factor(sample_conditions, levels = group_names)
TotalIntensitiesDF <- TotalIntensitiesDF[order(TotalIntensitiesDF$total_intensity), ]

# Creating ggplot bar graph, on a full-width row: its width grows with the number of samples (25 px per bar), so that the sample
# names keep a readable size (shrunk to the page width beyond about 40 samples)
total_intensity_width <- max(600, 25 * length(sample_names) + 100)

M_intensity_comparison <- ggplot(data = TotalIntensitiesDF) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity",aes(x=sample, y=total_intensity, fill = .data[[if (color_group) "condition" else "sample"]]))+
  scale_x_discrete(limits = as.character(TotalIntensitiesDF$sample)) +
  ggtitle("Total intensity across runs") +
  ylab("Total intensity")+
  xlab("")+
  {if(color_group) scale_fill_manual("Condition", values = setNames(group_colors, group_names))} +
  {if (color_group) condition_legend_guide(group_names, total_intensity_width, "fill")} +
  theme(legend.position = if (color_group) "bottom" else "none",
        legend.title=element_text(size=14),
        legend.text=element_text(size=13),
        plot.title = element_text(size=18),
        axis.title=element_text(size=16),
        axis.text=element_text(size=14),
        axis.text.x=element_text(angle=90, hjust=1, vjust=0.5, size=sample_axis_text_size(length(sample_names), total_intensity_width - 80, sample_names)))

##Plotting and printing 'Total intensity across runs' bar graph into html (.svg or .png dependent on set parameters) with download link##

cat(htmltools::HTML(plot_figure_as_html(M_intensity_comparison, "Total_intensity_across_runs", total_intensity_width, 600, svg = format_svg)))
figure_note("Total intensity of each sample (sum of all its observed intensities) before normalization, sorted from the lowest to the highest. It shows the differences of total measured signal between samples: a sample with a lower total can come from a lower protein amount (biological sample collection), a sample preparation issue or a loss of sensitivity of the mass spectrometer. It also decreases with the number of proteins quantified, and is dominated by the most abundant proteins. Moderate differences are corrected by the normalization.")
```

```{r correlation_plot, results='asis'}
##If the number of samples < 16 AND the data for each sample is < 5000 rows, a scatterplot of pairwise comparisons is framed##
##Else, a heatplot of correlated coefficients is framed##

# Full-width row: square figure growing with the number of samples, and with the width of their names for the heatmap (measured, see
# text_width_px in the library), shrunk to the page width if wider
use_ggpairs <- length(sample_names)<16 & nrow(data)<5000
names_width_at_10 <- max(text_width_px(sample_names, 10))
legend_width <- text_width_px("Correlation coefficient", 14) + 30
correlation_size <- if (use_ggpairs) max(600, 60 * length(sample_names)) else
  max(700, 25 * length(sample_names) + 1.4 * names_width_at_10 + legend_width + 100)

if (use_ggpairs){
  correlogram = ggpairs(log_abundance,title="Sample correlation",upper=list(continuous=wrap("cor",size=4)),lower=list(continuous=wrap("points",size=0.15))) +
    theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 10),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 18))
}else{
  cormat <- round(cor(log_abundance,use = "complete.obs"),2)
  #cormat = melt(cormat)
  cormat <- reshape2::melt(cormat)
  colnames(cormat) = c("Samples1","Samples2","Coefficient")
  # Sample label size: the names on the left (their width grows with the size) and the legend take part of the figure width, and the
  # columns need 1.25 times the size each: size <= (width - legend - margins) / (1.25 x samples + name width per pt), at most 14 pt
  label_size <- max(6, min(14, (correlation_size - legend_width - 60) / (1.25 * length(sample_names) + names_width_at_10 / 10)))
  correlogram = ggplot(data = cormat, aes(x=Samples1, y=Samples2, fill=Coefficient)) +
    geom_tile() +
    # Sequential scale over the observed coefficients (white = lowest, red = 1), so that the outlier samples stand out
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "red") +
    xlab("")+
    ylab("")+
    ggtitle("Sample correlation") +
    labs(fill = "Correlation coefficient") +
    theme(plot.title=element_text(size=18),
        axis.title=element_text(size=16),
        axis.text.y=element_text(size=label_size),
        axis.text.x=element_text(angle=90, hjust=1, vjust=0.5, size=label_size),
        legend.title=element_text(size=14),
        legend.text = element_text(size=13))
}

##Plotting and printing the 'sample correlation' plot into html (.svg or .png dependent on set parameters) with download link##

cat(htmltools::HTML(plot_figure_as_html(correlogram, "Sample_correlation", correlation_size, correlation_size, svg = format_svg)))
if (use_ggpairs){
  figure_note("Pairwise comparison of the samples on the log10 intensities: scatter plots (below the diagonal), Pearson correlation coefficients (above) and intensity distributions (diagonal). Replicates of the same condition should have the highest correlations; a sample less correlated with all the others is a possible outlier.")
} else {
  figure_note("Pearson correlation coefficients between the samples, computed on the log10 intensities of the proteins quantified in every sample (white: lowest coefficient, red: 1). Replicates of the same condition should have the highest correlations; a light row and column point to a sample less correlated with all the others, a possible outlier.")
}
```

```{r identification_type_plot, results='asis'}

## Number of proteins identified (by MS/MS) and quantified (by MS/MS or by matching) in each sample ##

identification_type = data[,grepl("Identification_type_",names(data)), drop = FALSE]

if(ncol(identification_type)>0){

  # Short sample name of each identification type column (same order as the sample columns)
  id_samples <- sapply(colnames(identification_type), function(col) as.character(namesDF$Id[namesDF$Sample == sub("^Identification_type_", "", col)]))

  # Counts per sample, among the proteins quantified in the sample (with an intensity): identified = by MS/MS, the others are
  # quantified without MS/MS identification. The identification type alone is not used for "quantified", as it can be given
  # for a protein without intensity (e.g. Proline derives it from the PSM count).
  quantified <- sapply(id_samples, function(s) { x <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(data[[s]])); !is.na(x) & x > 0 })
  msms <- as.matrix(identification_type) == "By MS/MS"
  msms[is.na(msms)] <- FALSE
  id_counts <- data.frame(
    sample = factor(id_samples, levels = id_samples),
    msms = colSums(quantified & msms),
    total = colSums(quantified),
    row.names = NULL)
  id_counts$other <- id_counts$total - id_counts$msms

  # One row per sample and type for the stacked bars (identified by MS/MS at the bottom)
  id_long <- rbind(data.frame(sample = id_counts$sample, type = "Identified (by MS/MS)", count = id_counts$msms),
                   data.frame(sample = id_counts$sample, type = "Quantified without MS/MS identification", count = id_counts$other))
  id_long$type <- factor(id_long$type, levels = c("Quantified without MS/MS identification", "Identified (by MS/MS)"))
  id_type_colors <- c("Identified (by MS/MS)" = "dodgerblue4", "Quantified without MS/MS identification" = "dodgerblue1")

  # Condition of each sample, when an experimental design is given
  id_has_design <- length(sample_conditions) == nrow(id_counts)
  if (id_has_design) id_counts$condition <- factor(sample_conditions, levels = unique(sample_conditions))
  id_max <- max(id_counts$total)
  # Coloured by condition (color_group): the bars take the colour of their condition, the MS/MS segment solid and the other one lighter,
  # with an outline. Otherwise: one blue per type, and a colored mark under each bar for the condition when a design is given.
  id_by_condition <- id_has_design && color_group
  if (id_by_condition) id_long$condition <- id_counts$condition[match(id_long$sample, id_counts$sample)]

  # Width growing with the number of samples (25 px per bar), so that the sample names and the counts keep a readable size
  n_id_samples <- nrow(id_counts)
  id_width <- max(600, 25 * n_id_samples + 100)
  id_height <- 650
  id_label_size <- sample_axis_text_size(n_id_samples, id_width - 80, as.character(id_counts$sample))
  # Counts (vertical) as thick as the bars allow, at most 12 pt (geom sizes are in mm: pt / .pt)
  id_count_pt <- max(6, min(12, (id_width - 100) / n_id_samples * 0.9 / 1.3))
  id_count_size <- id_count_pt / ggplot2::.pt
  # Room above the bars for the totals, written vertically: their measured width, relative to the height of the panel (figure height
  # minus the title, the sample names and the legends, measured or estimated)
  id_legend_rows <- if (id_by_condition) 2 + ceiling(length(group_names) / max(1, floor((id_width - 40) / (max(text_width_px(group_names, 13)) + 35)))) else 2
  id_panel_px <- id_height - 60 - max(text_width_px(as.character(id_counts$sample), id_label_size)) - 30 * id_legend_rows
  id_total_px <- max(text_width_px(id_counts$total, id_count_pt)) + 10
  id_top_expansion <- min(0.6, id_total_px / max(100, id_panel_px - id_total_px))
  # Legend of the two types (long texts), wrapping as the legend of the conditions
  id_types <- rev(names(id_type_colors))
  id_type_ncol <- max(1, min(2, floor((id_width - 40) / (max(text_width_px(id_types, 13)) + 35))))

  identification_type_plot = ggplot(id_long, aes(x = sample, y = count)) +
    {if (id_by_condition) geom_col(aes(fill = condition, alpha = type, colour = condition), width = 0.9, linewidth = 0.3)
     else geom_col(aes(fill = type), width = 0.9)} +
    {if (id_by_condition) list(scale_fill_manual("Condition", values = setNames(group_colors, group_names)),
                               scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(group_colors, group_names), guide = "none"),
                               scale_alpha_manual("", values = c("Identified (by MS/MS)" = 1, "Quantified without MS/MS identification" = 0.3),
                                                  breaks = id_types,
                                                  guide = guide_legend(ncol = id_type_ncol, override.aes = list(fill = "grey30", colour = "grey30"))),
                               condition_legend_guide(group_names, id_width, "fill"))
     else scale_fill_manual("", values = id_type_colors, breaks = id_types, guide = guide_legend(ncol = id_type_ncol))} +
    # Number identified by MS/MS, inside the MS/MS segment, and number quantified, above the bar (on a white background, readable on
    # any bar colour)
    geom_label(data = id_counts, aes(x = sample, y = msms, label = msms), angle = 90, hjust = 1.05, colour = "grey10", fill = "white",
               alpha = 0.8, label.size = 0, label.padding = unit(0.1, "lines"), size = id_count_size, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    geom_text(data = id_counts, aes(x = sample, y = total, label = total), angle = 90, hjust = -0.1, colour = "grey20", size = id_count_size,
              inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    {if (id_has_design && !id_by_condition) geom_point(data = id_counts, aes(x = sample, y = -0.03 * id_max, colour = condition), shape = 15, size = 3, inherit.aes = FALSE)} +
    {if (id_has_design && !id_by_condition) labs(colour = "Condition")} +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, id_top_expansion))) +
    xlab("") +
    ylab("Number of proteins") +
    ggtitle("Identified and quantified proteins per sample") +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size=fit_text_size("Identified and quantified proteins per sample", id_width - 60, 18)),
          axis.title=element_text(size=16),
          axis.text.x=element_text(angle=90, hjust=1, vjust=0.5, size=id_label_size),
          axis.text.y=element_text(size=14),
          legend.position="bottom",
          legend.box="vertical",
          legend.title=element_text(size=14),
          legend.text=element_text(size=13))

  cat(htmltools::HTML(plot_figure_as_html(identification_type_plot, "Identification_types_distribution_across_samples", id_width, id_height, svg = format_svg)))
  cat(text_spec(paste0("\n Number of proteins quantified in each sample (with an intensity: bar height, number above the bar), and among them the proteins ",
                       "identified by MS/MS in that sample (", if (id_by_condition) "solid part" else "dark blue", ", number inside the bar). The others (",
                       if (id_by_condition) "light part" else "light blue", ") are quantified without MS/MS identification ",
                       "in the sample (e.g. by matching). A sample with clearly fewer identifications than the other samples of its condition may indicate a problem with that injection.",
                       if (id_by_condition) " The bars have the colour of the condition of the sample." else if (id_has_design) " The colored mark under each bar gives the condition of the sample." else ""),
                italic = T, font_size = "12px"))
}
```

```{r normalization}

##Parsing from data file for normalization of samples##

na_count_by_sample = unname(colSums(is.na(as.matrix(data[,sample_names]))))
na_by_sample = data.frame(na_count_by_sample,sample_names)

# Extract raw intensities
raw_abundance = data[sample_names]

if (Normalization){
  
  # Find the sample with less NA
  reference_sample = subset(na_by_sample,na_by_sample$na_count_by_sample==min(na_by_sample$na_count_by_sample))$sample_names[1]
  
  # Normalization
  intensities_to_normalize = cbind(data$Id,raw_abundance)
  colnames(intensities_to_normalize)[1] = "Id"
  normalized_abundance = normalize(intensities_to_normalize,reference_sample)
  
  data = cbind(data,normalized_abundance[,-1])
  
  pattern = "_norm"
  
}else{
  
  pattern = ""
}

```

```{r plot_ratios, messages=FALSE, results='asis'}
##If normalization parameter set to TRUE, creating a data frame for 'Ratio distribution for each sample' ratio plot##

if(Normalization){
  ratiosDF = normalized_abundance[,grepl("_ratio_",names(normalized_abundance))]
  ratiosDF = data.table::melt.data.table(data.table(ratiosDF))
  colnames(ratiosDF) = c("samples","ratio")
  
  # Sample of each ratio (the column names are "<sample>_ratio_<reference sample>"): the plain sample names are shown on the axis,
  # the reference sample in the title
  ratiosDF$sample <- droplevels(factor(sub("_ratio_.*","",ratiosDF$samples), as.character(sample_names)))

  # Coloured by condition (color_group), with a legend of the conditions; otherwise one colour per sample, no legend
  if (color_group) ratiosDF$condition <- factor(sample_conditions[match(ratiosDF$sample, sample_names)], levels = group_names)

  # Full-width row: the width grows with the number of samples (25 px per box), so that the sample names keep a readable size
  n_ratio_samples <- nlevels(ratiosDF$sample)
  ratio_width <- max(600, 25 * n_ratio_samples + 100)

  ##Framing 'Ratio distribution for each sample' ratio plot using ggplot##

  ratioPlot <- ggplot() +
    geom_boxplot(data = ratiosDF, mapping = aes(x=sample, y=log2(ratio), color=.data[[if (color_group) "condition" else "sample"]], group=sample), na.rm = T) +
    # The reference sample in the subtitle (a long name would cut the title)
    labs(title = "Ratio distribution for each sample", subtitle = paste0("Ratios to the reference sample ", reference_sample)) +
    ylab("log2(ratio)") +
    xlab("") +
    # Without colouring by condition, the colours of the samples in the other plots (the reference sample has no ratio: ggplot's default
    # colours of the remaining samples would be shifted)
    {if(color_group) scale_color_manual("Condition", values = setNames(group_colors, group_names))
     else scale_color_manual(values = setNames(sample_palette, sample_names))} +
    {if (color_group) condition_legend_guide(group_names, ratio_width)} +
    theme(legend.position = if (color_group) "bottom" else "none",
        legend.title=element_text(size=14),
        legend.text=element_text(size=13),
        plot.title=element_text(size=18),
        plot.subtitle=element_text(size=14),
        axis.title=element_text(size=16),
        axis.text.x=element_text(angle=90, hjust=1, vjust=0.5, size=sample_axis_text_size(n_ratio_samples, ratio_width - 80, levels(ratiosDF$sample))),
        axis.text.y=element_text(size=14))

  ##Plotting and printing 'Ratio distribution for each sample' ratio plot (.svg or .png dependent on set parameters) with download link##

  cat(htmltools::HTML(plot_figure_as_html(ratioPlot, "Ratio_distribution_for_each_sample", ratio_width, 600, svg = format_svg)))
  figure_note(paste0("Distribution of the log2 ratios of the intensities of each sample to those of the reference sample (", reference_sample,
                     ", the sample with the fewest missing values), protein by protein, before normalization. The median of each box is the shift ",
                     "removed by the normalization; a wide box means that the sample differs from the reference for many proteins."))

}
```

```{r missing_values_imputation, results='asis'}
##Checks if normalized abundance data exists##

if(exists('normalized_abundance') && is.data.frame(get('normalized_abundance'))){
  data_to_impute = cbind.data.frame(data$Id,normalized_abundance)
}else{
  data_to_impute = cbind.data.frame(data$Id,raw_abundance)
}

##Creating data frame for 'Log intensities distribution with imputed values' histogram##

# Imputation with the noise model of the library (see estimate_noise_model). The noise sd is estimated within conditions when an
# experimental design is given, and over all the samples (one group) otherwise. If the model cannot be estimated (too few
# low-intensity proteins), the missing values are replaced by the percentile of each sample.
has_design_for_imputation <- length(sample_conditions) == ncol(data_to_impute) - 1
imputation_groups <- if (has_design_for_imputation) sample_conditions else rep("all samples", ncol(data_to_impute) - 1)
percentile <- Imputation.MNAR.percentile/100

noise_model <- tryCatch(estimate_noise_model(data_to_impute, imputation_groups, percentile), error = function(e) e)
if (inherits(noise_model, "error")) {
  imputed_samples = impute_using_noise_percentile(data_to_impute, percentile)
  imputation_text <- paste0("Missing values are replaced by the ", Imputation.MNAR.percentile, "% percentile of the observed intensities of each sample (the noise model could not be estimated: ",
                            sub("\\.$", "", sub("^Imputation: ", "", sub(" Use the percentile model.*$", "", conditionMessage(noise_model)))), ").")
} else {
  imputed_samples = impute_using_noise_model(data_to_impute, imputation_groups, noise_model, seed = 1)
  imputation_text <- paste0("Missing values are imputed with the noise model: values are drawn around the noise level of each sample (the ",
                            Imputation.MNAR.percentile, "% percentile of its observed intensities) with a standard deviation of ",
                            formatC(noise_model$noise_sd, format = "f", digits = 2), " log2, estimated on ", noise_model$n_rows, " low-intensity protein measurements ",
                            ifelse(has_design_for_imputation, "within conditions.", "over all the samples taken as one group (no experimental design was given, so the standard deviation may include differences between conditions)."),
                            " The imputation uses a fixed seed and is reproducible.")
}
data = cbind(data,imputed_samples)

#####imputed_samples_log = imputed_samples

#####imputed_samples_log[,1:ncol(imputed_samples_log)] = log10(imputed_samples_log)
imputed_samples_log <- imputed_samples
imputed_samples_log[imputed_samples_log == 0] <- 1e-8
imputed_samples_log <- log10(imputed_samples_log)

colnames(imputed_samples_log)[1:ncol(imputed_samples_log)] = paste0(colnames(imputed_samples_log)[1:ncol(imputed_samples_log)],"_log")
data = cbind(data,imputed_samples_log)

# Make a data frame of values to plot
imputed_abundance = data[,grepl("_imputed_log",names(data)), drop = FALSE]
imputedIntensityDF = reshape2::melt(imputed_abundance)
colnames(imputedIntensityDF) = c("sample","log10_intensity")
imputedIntensityDF$sample = sub("_imputed_log","",imputedIntensityDF$sample)

# Build NA mask from raw_abundance for the SAME sample columns (and same order)
raw_mat <- raw_abundance[, sample_names, drop = FALSE]         # exclude Id
na_mask <- is.na(raw_mat)

# Melt mask and attach (same ordering if columns align)
imputedFlagDF <- reshape2::melt(na_mask)
imputedIntensityDF$imputed <- imputedFlagDF$value

## imputed? (one flag per protein and sample, in the same order as reshape2::melt(imputed_abundance), i.e. sample by sample)
imputed = as.vector(na_mask)
## final dataframe
#imputedIntensityDF <- data.frame(imputedIntensityDF,imputed)


##Framing 'Log intensities distribution with imputed values' histogram using ggplot##
histogram <- ggplot() +
  geom_histogram(data = imputedIntensityDF, mapping = aes(x = log10_intensity, fill = imputed), alpha=0.7, bins = 100) +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("dodgerblue3", "darkorchid4"))+
  ggtitle("Log intensities distribution with imputed values") +
  xlab("log(intensity)")+
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size=18),
        axis.title=element_text(size=16),
        axis.text=element_text(size=14),
        legend.title = element_text(size=14),
        legend.text = element_text(size=13))

##Plotting and printing 'Log intensities distribution with imputed values' histogram to html doc (.svg or .png dependent on set parameters)##
##with download link##

  # Full-width row
  htmltools::HTML(plot_figure_as_html(histogram, "Log_intensities_distribution_with_imputed_values", 1100, 600, svg = format_svg))

##Prints explanation of histogram data##

cat(text_spec(paste0("\n ", imputation_text),italic=T,font_size="12px"))
```

<div id="banner">
# **Dimension reduction**
</div>
<br>

```{r pca_compute, echo=FALSE}
## PCA of the samples: samples are the observations, proteins the variables ##

# Log10 intensities after normalization (if enabled) and imputation, one column per sample
pca_matrix <- as.matrix(imputed_abundance)
colnames(pca_matrix) <- sample_names

# Values that were missing before imputation, and number of quantified proteins per sample (proteome depth)
missing_before_imputation <- is.na(as.matrix(raw_abundance[sample_names]))
n_quantified <- colSums(!missing_before_imputation)
pct_imputed <- round(100 * mean(missing_before_imputation), 1)

# Main PCA: each protein centered, not scaled (more variable proteins weigh more)
pca_main <- compute_sample_pca(pca_matrix)

# Scaled PCA: each protein centered and scaled to unit variance (every protein weighs the same)
pca_scaled <- compute_sample_pca(pca_matrix, scale = TRUE)

# Proteins with a non-finite value are left out of the PCA (see compute_sample_pca)
pca_matrix <- pca_matrix[apply(pca_matrix, 1, function(x) all(is.finite(x))), , drop = FALSE]
pca_subtitle <- paste0(pca_main$n_proteins, " proteins, ", pct_imputed, "% of the values imputed")

# Sample annotations (condition and replicate are known only when an experimental design is given)
pca_samples <- data.frame(sample = sample_names, n_quantified = n_quantified, row.names = NULL)
has_design <- length(sample_conditions) == length(sample_names)
if (has_design) {
  pca_samples$condition <- factor(sample_conditions, levels = unique(sample_conditions))
  pca_samples$replicate <- factor(sample_replicates, levels = unique(sample_replicates))
}

# Colors of the conditions (variance_explained and plot_pca_samples are in the library)
pca_colors <- if (color_group) setNames(group_colors, group_names) else NULL

```

```{r pca_scaled_plot, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
htmltools::HTML(plot_figure_as_html(plot_pca_samples(pca_scaled, pca_samples, "PCA of the samples, proteins scaled (technical view)", pca_subtitle, pca_colors), "PCA_samples_scaled", 700, 700, svg = format_svg))
cat(text_spec("\n Log10 intensities, each protein centered and scaled to unit variance, so all proteins weigh the same, including the many proteins that do not change. Their technical noise then has as much weight as the biological changes: this view helps to detect technical effects (injection order, batches), not biological ones.", italic = T, font_size = "12px"))
```
</div>
</div>

```{r pca_depth, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
## Do the first components follow the proteome depth of the samples? ##

depth_df <- rbind(
  data.frame(pca_samples, component = "PC1", score = pca_main$x[, 1]),
  data.frame(pca_samples, component = "PC2", score = pca_main$x[, 2])
)
depth_r <- c(PC1 = cor(pca_main$x[, 1], n_quantified), PC2 = cor(pca_main$x[, 2], n_quantified))
depth_df$component <- factor(depth_df$component, levels = c("PC1", "PC2"),
                             labels = paste0(c("PC1", "PC2"), " (r = ", round(depth_r, 2), ")"))

depth_plot <- ggplot(depth_df, aes(x = n_quantified, y = score)) +
  {if (has_design) geom_point(aes(colour = condition), size = 3) else geom_point(size = 3)} +
  {if (has_design && color_group) scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(group_colors, group_names))} +
  # Full-width row: PC1 and PC2 side by side
  facet_wrap(~component, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Components vs proteome depth", x = "Number of quantified proteins (before imputation)", y = "Sample score", colour = "Condition") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 18),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 13))

htmltools::HTML(plot_figure_as_html(depth_plot, "PCA_vs_proteome_depth", 1100, 550, svg = format_svg))
cat(text_spec("\n Sample scores of the main PCA against the number of proteins quantified in each sample. A strong correlation (|r| close to 1) means that the component mostly reflects differences in proteome depth (and therefore imputed values) rather than biology.", italic = T, font_size = "12px"))
```
</div>
</div>

```{r pca_scree, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
## Variance explained by the first components of both PCAs ##

n_components <- min(10, length(pca_main$sdev))
scree_df <- rbind(
  data.frame(pca = "Main PCA", component = seq_len(n_components), variance = variance_explained(pca_main)[seq_len(n_components)]),
  data.frame(pca = "Proteins scaled", component = seq_len(n_components), variance = variance_explained(pca_scaled)[seq_len(n_components)])
)

scree_plot <- ggplot(scree_df, aes(x = factor(component), y = variance)) +
  geom_col(fill = "dodgerblue3") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(variance, 1), "%")), vjust = -0.4, size = 5) +
  facet_wrap(~pca, ncol = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))) +
  labs(title = "Variance explained", x = "Component", y = "% of variance") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 18),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 14))

# Half-width column, next to the table of the loadings: 600 px, so that it is not shrunk
cat(htmltools::HTML(plot_figure_as_html(scree_plot, "PCA_variance_explained", 600, 650, svg = format_svg)))
figure_note("Percentage of the variance of the samples explained by each of the first components, for both PCAs. A first component well above the others means that one main effect (e.g. the conditions, or a technical effect) dominates the differences between samples.")
```
</div>

<div class = "col-md-6">
```{r pca_top_loadings, echo=FALSE}
## Proteins contributing most to the first two components of the main PCA ##

# Protein labels: gene name when available, accession otherwise
protein_labels <- as.character(data$Id)
if ("Accession" %in% colnames(data)) protein_labels <- as.character(data$Accession)
if ("Gene_name" %in% colnames(data)) {
  has_gene <- !is.na(data$Gene_name) & data$Gene_name != ""
  protein_labels[has_gene] <- as.character(data$Gene_name[has_gene])
}
names(protein_labels) <- rownames(imputed_abundance)
loadings_labels <- protein_labels[rownames(pca_matrix)]

top_loadings <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("PC1", "PC2"), function(pc) {
  l <- pca_main$rotation[, pc]
  top <- order(abs(l), decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(min(10, length(l)))]
  data.frame(Component = pc, Rank = seq_along(top), Protein = loadings_labels[top], Loading = round(l[top], 3), row.names = NULL)
}))

kable(top_loadings, format = "html", booktabs = T,
      caption = "Proteins with the largest loadings on PC1 and PC2 of the main PCA (the sign gives the direction along the component)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "condensed", full_width = F, position = "left") %>%
  collapse_rows(columns = 1, valign = "top")
```
</div>

<div id="banner">
# **Hierarchical clustering**
</div>
<br>

```{r heatmaps, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='asis'}
## Heatmaps of all the proteins in each sample, with the proteins and the samples ordered by hierarchical clustering
## (see plot_clustered_heatmap in the library): log10 intensities, then z-scores of each protein ##

# Log10 intensities after normalization (if enabled) and imputation, one column per sample. The imputed values are used by the
# clusterings (a complete matrix is needed) but are left blank in the heatmaps
heatmap_values <- as.matrix(imputed_abundance)
colnames(heatmap_values) <- sample_names
n_heatmap_samples <- length(sample_names)

# Orientation: proteins in rows when they need more room than the samples (usual case), samples in rows otherwise (many samples).
# The sample axis grows with the number of samples (25 px per sample, at most 2400 px) so that the names stay readable; the heatmap
# itself takes about 7/8 of the height or 8/9 of the width left by the legend.
proteins_in_rows <- heatmap_proteins_in_rows(nrow(heatmap_values), n_heatmap_samples)
sample_axis_px <- min(2400, max(700, 25 * n_heatmap_samples + 300))
if (proteins_in_rows) {
  heatmap_width <- sample_axis_px; heatmap_height <- 950
  heatmap_label_size <- sample_axis_text_size(n_heatmap_samples, (heatmap_width - 150) * 8 / 9, sample_names)
} else {
  heatmap_width <- 1300; heatmap_height <- sample_axis_px
  heatmap_label_size <- sample_axis_text_size(n_heatmap_samples, (heatmap_height - 100) * 7 / 8)
}
heatmap_axes <- if (proteins_in_rows) "all the proteins (rows) in each sample (columns)" else "all the proteins (columns) in each sample (rows)"
heatmap_dendrograms <- if (proteins_in_rows) "dendrograms of the proteins on the left and of the samples above" else "dendrograms of the samples on the left and of the proteins above"

intensity_heatmap <- plot_clustered_heatmap(heatmap_values, blank = missing_before_imputation, title = "Log10 intensities",
                                            fill_label = "log10(intensity)", label_size = heatmap_label_size, proteins_in_rows = proteins_in_rows)

# Centered values (as the main PCA): each protein centered across the samples, as log2, i.e. the log2 fold change of each value to the
# average of its protein. The proteins that change most stand out, the stable ones stay pale. Own clusterings, computed on these values,
# and colors limited to +/- 2 (4-fold), so that a few extreme proteins do not flatten the scale.
centered_values <- (heatmap_values - rowMeans(heatmap_values)) * log2(10)
centered_heatmap <- plot_clustered_heatmap(centered_values, blank = missing_before_imputation, title = "Centered log2 intensities",
                                           subtitle = "Log2 fold change to the protein average - as the main PCA",
                                           fill_label = "log2 fold change", limits = c(-2, 2), label_size = heatmap_label_size, proteins_in_rows = proteins_in_rows)

# Z-scores: each protein centered and scaled across the samples (the proteins with the same value in every sample have no z-score
# and are left out). The heatmap has its own clusterings, computed on the z-scores, and its colors are centered on 0 and limited
# to +/- 3, so that a few extreme values do not flatten the scale.
zscore_heatmap <- plot_clustered_heatmap(t(scale(t(heatmap_values))), blank = missing_before_imputation, title = "Z-scored log10 intensities",
                                         subtitle = "As the scaled PCA (technical view)",
                                         fill_label = "z-score", limits = c(-3, 3), label_size = heatmap_label_size, proteins_in_rows = proteins_in_rows)

## Heatmaps printed into the report (PNG or SVG, see plot_figure_as_html) ##

cat(htmltools::HTML(plot_figure_as_html(intensity_heatmap, "global_hcplot", heatmap_width, heatmap_height, svg = format_svg)))
figure_note(paste0("Log10 intensities", if (Normalization) " after normalization" else "", " of ", heatmap_axes, ", from green (low) to red (high); missing values that were imputed are left blank. ",
                   "Proteins and samples are ordered by hierarchical clustering (", heatmap_dendrograms, "): samples of the same condition should cluster together. ",
                   "The proteins are mostly ordered by abundance here, as their intensity levels differ much more than their variations between samples."))
# Space between the heatmaps, so that they are clearly separated
heatmap_space <- "<div style='height: 60px;'></div>"
cat(heatmap_space)
cat(htmltools::HTML(plot_figure_as_html(centered_heatmap, "global_hcplot_centered", heatmap_width, heatmap_height, svg = format_svg)))
figure_note(paste0("Log2 fold change of each value to the average of its protein over the samples (each protein centered, as in the main PCA): green, lower than the average; red, higher ",
                   "(colors limited to 4-fold). The proteins that change most between samples stand out, the stable ones stay pale. The proteins and the samples are ordered by a hierarchical ",
                   "clustering of these values: blocks of proteins higher or lower in a group of samples show the main differences between conditions."))
cat(heatmap_space)
cat(htmltools::HTML(plot_figure_as_html(zscore_heatmap, "global_hcplot_scored", heatmap_width, heatmap_height, svg = format_svg)))
figure_note(paste0("Intensities of each protein z-scored (centered and scaled across the samples, as in the scaled PCA), so that every protein weighs the same ",
                   "(green: lower than its average, red: higher; colors limited to 3 standard deviations). The many proteins that do not change are amplified to the same level as those that change: ",
                   "this technical view helps to detect effects on all the proteins (injection order, batches, an outlier sample), the previous heatmap the biological differences. ",
                   "The proteins and the samples are ordered by a hierarchical clustering of the z-scores."))

```
